evidence.title: Correction: a later host burst overflows the pipeline queue while the 4 MiB ring stays clean
evidence.description: After the ring deploy's 180 s clean window (drops 0 over 178,499 rows), a subsequent host burst pushed the 16,384-slot pipeline queue to its reserve boundary: dropped_total reached 10,408 (capture_fim 9,553, capture_etw 855) with minifilter ring drops still 0, and readiness returned to degraded=true / overall_gate=false. A 60 s follow-up sampling found the drop counter frozen (no ongoing loss) while depth oscillated between 19 and 12,469, i.e. one absorbed burst that exceeded available headroom, not a sustained throughput deficit (rows were draining ~992-1,250/s).
tests: 20-sample burst watch after the episode: dropped_total constant, depth 19..12,469
ring_dropped=0 throughout the burst

evidence.finding: The queue's burst headroom is insufficient on this host: 16,384 slots (~26 MB of static state at ~1.6 KB/slot) minus the 1,024 reserved network tail left host telemetry refused during a single spike. This is a real loss and is recorded as OPEN rather than hidden behind the earlier zero window. Next slice must size capacity from a measured peak depth through a burst, or coalesce repeated FIM events for the same path at ingress; raising the queue alone must be justified by memory cost.

evidence.title: Bounded diagnostic-log rotation closes unbounded growth that filled the system drive
evidence.description: The persisted diagnostic stream (RB013-LOG TeeSink -> <exe_dir>/../logs/aegis-daemon-diagnostic.log) had no size bound. On the production host that file reached 40.9 GB (40,921,296,585 bytes at capture) and drove C: to 0 bytes free, breaking unrelated tooling that stages output under the system temp directory. FileSink now rotates at DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES = 64 MiB, keeps exactly one backup at <path>.1 (total bounded by two caps), and rotates a legacy oversized file on the first write after restart so deploying the build stops growth without a manual delete. The sink owns its path copy and frees it in deinit; path-less synthetic sinks keep the previous behaviour.

zig build test --summary all: 2,036 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed
FileSink rotates at the byte cap and keeps one backup
FileSink rotates a legacy oversized file on the first write
evidence.finding: In-tree fix proven at E2 only. The installed host still runs the f7c626d image with the unbounded sink and the 40.9 GB file is still present; stopping the growth and reclaiming the space needs an owner-approved elevated deploy and an explicit delete of the stale file. Raw log growth also indicates the diagnostic stream is far too verbose per captured packet, which the QLOSS admission work should address separately.

evidence.title: BUILD-001: artifact digests made checkout-line-ending independent
evidence.description: file_sha256 previously hashed raw working-tree bytes, so every digest depended on the checkout's line endings. That is why CI carried a 'Regenerate manifest to match CI working tree' step: the drift gate was being satisfied by rewriting the manifest rather than by detecting drift. Hashing now normalizes CRLF to LF for non-binary files (binary files, detected by NUL, are hashed verbatim), and `size` records the normalized length so size and digest always agree. .gitattributes (* text eol=lf) is now the single source of line-ending truth. All 279 recorded digests were recomputed once via --refresh-digests.

Follow-up (same day): the sensor pipe is PIPE_UNLIMITED_INSTANCES (nids_capture.zig:188) while the control pipe is max-1-instance. A stray second daemon therefore CAN co-create the sensor endpoint, splitting nose/event flow away from prod -- the hazard is not just a lingering process but potential silent event loss, so no isolated second daemon may run on the opened system without a daemon-wide test mode (alt sensor pipe + alt forensic log + alt control pipe). The 8s probe (pid 7728, killed) showed no lasting harm (prod pid 8736 RUNNING, 23 rules after), but the window existed. WFP side: provider_ready() returns 0 non-elevated with DLL + driver present, proving the remaining skip is privilege-gated, not file-gated.

known_gaps.finding: The >=1500-byte direct-capture window recorded in EVT-215 is NOT driver/path behavior -- mechanism superseded. Measured fresh: tshark on VMnet1 shows cap_len==len exact (10/10 sent broadcasts: 5x83 red, 5x75 plain); a raw ctypes probe of wpcap.dll reading the header THROUGH the returned pointer shows as16 layout exact (caplen@8 == len@12 == 83/83 and 75/75; the 24-byte reading is garbage); deployed aegis_nids.exe is byte-identical to the repo zig-out build (sha256 6D03115B71E3C9E70449D7DBDBB301FA04ACC0103799A89B94144692E1001630). known_gaps.title: L4 rules are per-packet predicates, not rate/window flood or scan detectors
known_gaps.description: R9006 fired on any exact SYN (normal handshakes included); R9002 on any ICMP echo/reply; R9007 on exact FIN+PSH+URG. No rate, window, or scan-pattern state existed at discovery. The rule names (TCP SYN Stealth Scan, ICMP Flood) implied rate semantics that were not implemented. The 2026-10-20 lab is explicit about this: a 100-port nmap scan produced 200 matching packets and 300 hping3 ICMP packets produced 300 rows -- per-packet matches, not flood/scan verdicts.
required_evidence: rate/window state and threshold tests for SYN/ICMP, or an explicit rename/reclassification to per-packet predicates
negative control showing normal handshakes/pings below a threshold do not fire
known_gaps.resolution: Implemented opt-in L4 rate/window semantics in src/pipeline/l4_matcher.zig, config-driven by configs/Rules.json. R9002: count >=50 ICMP packets per source per 1000 ms. R9006: >=20 distinct destination ports per source per 10000 ms. Both emit once per source/window; R9007 remains exact FIN|PSH|URG per-packet. The tracker keys rule + full source address + IPv4/IPv6 identity, is a fixed 256-entry table, and resets on rules reload. Zig tests cover the 49th-vs-50th ICMP boundary, 19-vs-20 distinct-port boundary, duplicate-port suppression, once-per-window emission/re-arm, source and address-family separation, reset, and the stateless R9007 path; negative controls prove a normal single handshake and sub-threshold pings do not fire. Config pins are in tests/security/test_l4_rate_config.py. This closes the code-semantics gap at E2; the installed 04F9... artifact (2026-10-20) later proved R9002 live at E5, while R9006/R9007 live proof is now recorded on the canonical Nose path and in the isolated lab.
